text: You're at the gate, ticket in hand, eager for your flight. All you want is to get on board, find your seat, and relax.
The call for your boarding group comes, and you join the line, expecting a smooth, efficient flow onto the plane.
But as you step inside, the process grinds to a halt. People struggle with bags, blocking the narrow aisle, and you wonder why it's always this slow.
The truth is, a plane is just a long, narrow tube. While many can board, only one person can effectively use the aisle at a time.
Every passenger needs to find their seat AND stow their luggage, turning the aisle into a series of mini-bottlenecks. This destroys true parallel boarding.
So next time you're stuck, remember it’s not just slow people. It’s the system's fundamental design, making true efficiency an illusion.
